the-vendor-strategy-partner-vs-utility.core: Choosing a vendor means buying a long-term dependency. Classify vendors as utilities (commodity, easily swapped, optimise on price) or partners (strategic, deeply integrated, invest in the relationship), and manage each accordingly.

first_principles.problem: Teams pick a critical vendor on a quick demo and price alone, then find themselves locked into a poor partnership for years.
derivation: Use a **selection rigour** that matches the stakes.

analogy.title: Choosing a business partner vs. a stationery supplier
analogy.story: You compare paper prices quickly; a business partner needs deep due diligence.
analogy.breaks: Vendors can move between categories as your dependence grows.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Effort spent where the stakes are high.

check.q: What distinguishes a 'partner' vendor from a 'utility' vendor?
check.a: Partners are strategic, deeply integrated and costly to replace; utilities are commodities that can be swapped on price.

the-rfp-process-the-bake-off.core: An RFP runs a fair, structured comparison. Define requirements and weighted criteria up front, send the same scenarios to all vendors, run a hands-on proof of concept (the bake-off) with your real data, and score independently.

first_principles.problem: Decisions are swayed by the slickest demo or the loudest internal advocate.
derivation: Run a **PoC** on your workloads (2–4 weeks).

analogy.title: A cooking competition with the same ingredients
analogy.story: Every chef gets the same basket and the judges score blind, so you see real skill.
analogy.breaks: RFPs can be slow and heavy, so scale them to the decision.

example.title: Scoring matrix
flow: Criteria: query perf 25%, cost 25%, integrations 20%, support 15%, security 15%

check.q: Why define weighted scoring criteria before seeing vendor demos?
check.a: To avoid being swayed by presentation and to compare vendors consistently against real needs.

the-pre-nup-designing-your-exit-strategy.core: Negotiate the exit before you sign: data export formats and timelines, termination-assistance clauses, price caps on renewal, SLA penalties and abstraction layers in your architecture. Lock-in isn't failure, but unplanned lock-in removes leverage.

first_principles.problem: At renewal the vendor raises prices 40%, and exporting your data turns out to be nearly impossible.
derivation: **Data portability**: export in open formats, at no cost, within X days.
**Renewal caps**: price increase ≤ X% per year.

analogy.title: A prenuptial agreement
analogy.story: Planned while everyone's friendly, it makes a future separation orderly.
analogy.breaks: Over-abstracting to avoid lock-in wastes the vendor's value, so balance them.

example.title: Negotiated exit terms
flow: Full data export in Parquet within 30 days on request

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Leverage kept for the whole relationship.

check.q: Why negotiate exit terms before signing a vendor contract?
check.a: Your leverage is highest before commitment, and switching costs and vendor power grow afterwards.

managing-the-ongoing-relationship-qbrs-a.core: The contract is day one. Manage strategic vendors actively with quarterly business reviews (usage, SLA performance, roadmap, issues), escalation paths, executive sponsors, usage monitoring to right-size renewals and credible alternatives to keep leverage.

first_principles.problem: Vendors are forgotten until renewal, when the company discovers it overpaid for unused licences and has no leverage.
derivation: Hold **QBRs**: SLA performance, support tickets, roadmap alignment.

analogy.title: Maintaining a landlord relationship
analogy.story: Regular check-ins, documented issues and knowledge of the local market make renewals fair.
analogy.breaks: Adversarial management harms partnerships, so be firm but collaborative.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: 30% saved at renewal and better support.

check.q: What's the purpose of a Quarterly Business Review with a vendor?
check.a: To review performance, usage and roadmap alignment regularly, resolve issues and keep leverage for renewals.
